cim: Artificial Intelligence should be nowhere near art
cim_eredeti: Artificial Intelligence should be nowhere near art
szoveg_eredeti:
Growing up, I refused to let myself be called an artist in any capacity. It wasn’t because I was ashamed of the title itself, but rather because I always felt that I hadn’t achieved the level of blood, sweat and tears to be allowed to call myself a “true” artist. I’ve found this sort of humbleness and criticism of one’s own work is a common trend with most artists, regardless of their medium. Its almost a rite of passage, if you will. With the recent rise of content generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), however, this rite of passage has been disgraced with an influx of people proudly calling themselves “AI artists.”

Although using AI to create content, such as art or music, may seem harmless in theory, it goes against the very core of what humanity is.

When it comes to AI, there are countless debates on when it should be used and how ethical its usage even is, considering that AI allows for nearly anything to be generated. From academic dishonesty in schools to the generation of fake videos supporting fake news, the reach and possibilities of AI are quite jarring to think about. To push it further, there is also the creation of disgusting content, such as AI-generated child sexual abuse material – which was ruled in late August by the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit to be legal and protected under the First Amendment right.

However, AI has the potential to be quite useful in STEM fields. It could effectively streamline calculations and data collecting, processing and analysis, allowing for scientists and researchers to get to the so-called “meat” of their work. This would lead to faster progressions in research that have the potential to lead to new, beneficial discussions.

Still, it is an undebatable truth that there is no place for AI in the arts. The arts is inherently a field full of passion, given that as a career, it is unfortunately more often than not a financially fruitless endeavor. Artists of all kinds are scarcely well-rewarded and are underpaid for the work that they do, which is keeping the heart of society and community alive. To create, entertain, sing, dance, draw, act, write, sculpt, paint, recite and build while placing a piece of one’s soul into each artwork is what it means to be an artist. That is why it is true sacrilege when people who use AI to “create” dare to coin themselves an artist.

Even though self-proclaimed “AI artists” often excuse their actions – quite proudly, I may add – by saying that AI is their only means to create, whether it be due to physical limitations or because they weren’t born with a natural talent, it doesn’t excuse anything at all. Most artists that I know, myself included, did not start off with some intrinsic ability to create beautiful works of art. It takes effort, patience and spirit to become an artist in any capacity.

There is always a way to create. It doesn’t matter if what you create is “good” or not; it matters that it is human. That is why AI-generated images could never be considered art.

AI-generated images steal from real-life artists. It takes their work and robs them of their heart. It robs humanity of its core.

Stop the use of AI. Stop the race to replace art. Stop the erasure of humanity.
